title: NATS Per-Service Identity + ACL Registry
description: Single source of truth for NATS per-service authentication. Validates infrastructure/nats/services.yaml. Consumed by the CI invariant test nats-invariants.spec.ts.

version.description: Schema version. Bump only on breaking shape changes; add migration notes in ADR-015.

services.description: Ordered list of NATS services. Order is preserved by the nats.conf generator for auditable diffs.

name.description: NATS user identifier. MUST exactly match the mTLS client cert CN for this service (verify_and_map maps CN → user). Lowercase snake_case.

application.description: Unique apps/<directory> runtime that owns this certificate identity. APP_TO_SERVICE and deploy invariants derive from this field; identities may not be shared.

description.description: One-line summary of what this service publishes/consumes. Appears in ADR and runbook generation.

publish.description: Explicit publish subjects. JetStream manager consumers require the exact $JS.API.INFO API; delivered-message replies use bounded responses permissions, never a shared inbox wildcard.

subscribe.description: Explicit subscribe subjects, including only this certificate identity's inbox and separately authorized domain inboxes. No global inbox subscription is permitted.

max.description: One terminal JetStream ACK or NAK per delivered message; unary Nest RPC responders allow a response plus a separately scheduled disposal frame.

expires.description: Finite delivered-reply grant lifetime in seconds. The generator requires exact agreement with libs/backend-common/src/nats/nats-response-policy.json; runtime RPC timeout validation consumes that same policy.

responses.description: Broker-scoped permission to answer only reply subjects of messages actually delivered to this connection. No unsolicited inbox publish or broad $JS.ACK permission.

subject.description: NATS subject pattern in a canonical platform namespace. The legacy AQUACULTURE_EVENTS. prefix is structurally rejected because it is a stream name, never a publish subject. Reply inboxes are per-service scoped (SEC-HIGH-098, 2026-08-23 scan №43): every service subscribes `_INBOX<SERVICE>.>` matching the connection factory's inboxPrefix — no cert can subscribe another service's reply stream. The dedicated secret-bearing prefixes `_INBOXBILLINGCFG.` / `_INBOXFARMMARINECFG.` remain additional restrictions inside that scheme.
